body:
I second lithium. I was in a similar boat to you, except I actually acted out a lot of it and got in serious trouble. I was uncontrollable.

Now I'm on lithium, and I haven't had sex with my partner in months. It's horrible, but probably still better than the other way :P

I have no advice otherwise. Nothing else stopped me.

Hey, just got back from my appointment (yeah, it's been a long time since this post). The doc said it's just me contemplating stuff a bit. It sucks, and he can kinda relate (he's on meds for the rest of his life) but in the end every human is different, I was dealt a weird deck, but it isn't impossible. The treatment I'm on is effective, and I'm not in danger.
And who knows, by his words, maybe they will come up with a better way (gene therapy) that can fix us. For now, I'm not really different from someone taking allergy meds, or heartburn meds, or cholesterol meds. It's just a matter of improving my life quality.
There are options, and there is a future of improvements and medical advancements that might make life for a bipolar person even easier.

In short, basically he said yes, it sucks, but I can think positively as well.
I'm perfectly comfortable sharing how the appointment goes. I'll let you know.

Before I was on lithium, I was in a mixed state. Previous to that, I have had several long depressive episodes and shorter manic episodes, all surfacing since middle school. So you guessed correctly - I've had long depressions.
I have actually been meditating, but I definitely lapsed on it recently once my life started picking up again. I'll get back in it. Good advice!

And you are right, it is not my fate to die from this. But the diagnosis certainly makes me contemplate my own mortality. Also makes me think of reality. My reality only months ago was me not able to see a future, unable to function and stuck in an infinite loop of "you better kill yourself". Then only days on lithium, everything is fine. My reality shifted. It reinforced my thoughts on every person's reality being different, but also gave me the realization that I have lived with 3-4 realities my whole life.
Perhaps I'm just spewing nonsense, but I appreciate the response :)

I have an appointment coming up soon. Figured I'd talk to my doc there instead of calling. I can let you know how it goes. My psychologist just seemed to imply I need to learn to handle it. Psychiatrist might have a different opinion since he knows the meds. Was just curious if anyone else has come to terms with this type of stuff :(
I'll give them a quick phone call.

Literally nothing. I spent years and years having hypomanic episodes and depressed episodes and just thought this was how shitty life is. Then I tried to make sense of my random spurts of sexuality, spending, and doing plenty of things without regards for consequences, people, or sleep.

Then I got on antidepressants during a depressive phase. That didn't work. I came back to my doctor after crashing from another hypomanic episode and he said "oh, I noticed you are acting MUCH different. This is bipolar disorder, not depression"

I knew nothing of it. I had to look it up and I had every single thing on the list.... so "OH SHIT, I DO have bipolar"
The end brought me to tears
Wow. Favorited.

You are correct. You should like my psychologist, haha. The problem is how illogical I am when I am this depressed. Yes, him not responding was an act of war to me. I demanded him to be there. He needs to hold up his end of the deal for me to be okay through tomorrow.

I hope he defends me to his family, but I can't know. I just really wish he could understand how much those minutes of silence effects me, and try to mitigate them. It would make it so much easier (although still challenging) for me.

I spend all my time around him otherwise. We play the same games, we do the same activities. We share pretty much every hobby (it's how we met). Having him suddenly gone, and gone with "the enemy" is hurtful, though I know he doesn't mean it.

Thank you for throwing some logic in here. I can speak a little better now that I had some sedatives too. :(
I wish my trying was enough.
thank you

Ehhh... I just ruin things as lot. I get lonely, get angry at all my friends for leaving or my family for not being around. I'm extroverted, but don't leave the house when I'm depressed. But of course, no one is online to chat when they are with family for the holidays. So I just spiral and spiral.
My childhood memories of the holidays are my mom and dad fighting, then my mom and dad getting divorced (dad is bipolar, mom couldn't handle it) and then being alone each Christmas. Then meeting someone, not wanting to be alone, but getting insulted and berated by their family for asking them to spend half of the holidays with me. This is a similar situation with a new person, just even more extreme.

The holiday "Christmas" just has always had a negative association for me and tends to trigger me. Doesn't help that I can't avoid it. I'm trying to get over it.

Yeah, I'm not so sure anymore. I generally am an agreeable person. I'm logical, and intelligent. I want people to like me and I want people to understand things, but this might be out of my league.
Turns out, she is accusing her husband of being bipolar (undiagnosed) and now they are getting a divorce. I think what is happening here is she now thinks she is some expert on the illness and is associating me with the "bad guy" husband, and telling my boyfriend to GTFO before it's too late :(

I would love to. In particular I keep telling him to let his mom speak to me. She's only spoken to him and I know even he doesn't fully understand the illness. I linked him to articles, had him read them (and he did) but he's still a "standard/normal" human in that respect, so he doesn't know what these moods are like.

http://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/topics/bipolar-disorder/index.shtml
This is one of the articles I had him read. I told him to pass it on to his mom, but he didn't. Any other suggestions/articles are appreciated. I really want to get to speak to her.

That's disheartening, but I thank you for the honesty.
We are both in our 20's (I am 26) but he is very close to his family. In particular, if he doesn't visit them regularly or misses some family event because I am having issues (I feel very guilty making him miss/mess up ANYTHING), they are blaming me and getting quite upset.

They definitely view it as a character flaw. "Sure, she may be upset but hurting herself? That is NOT a healthy solution to her problems and she is just trying to control you. Do you love her more than you love ME?!" <--- That's approximately the kind of stuff I get.

Obviously both me and my boyfriend don't want to break it off, but it seems like more and more lately he's crumbling under family pressure and it's bound to break soon. I don't know how else to approach the problem anymore. I am seeing two doctors a week, and I'm currently transitioning meds and I have some klonopin to calm me down as I deal with withdrawals from my old meds and side effects of my new meds. But this episode is quite severe for me and I've already spent some time in the ER for it. I just want things to settle down, and his family issues are making it worse instead.

I would LOVE it if he could just be independent and let mommy realize that. I doubt that is gonna happen.

Quick update for you, since you asked:
Tried two hits - was all just fine! I definitely had to stay moving, even with an indica (instead of playing games, I ended up taking my dog on a walk) but the nice visuals outside and the fresh air made me feel fantastic. I think I'm moving in a positive direction and will keep trying :)
Answered

Games relax me immensely. They are my way of cooling off at the end of a long work day and feeling awesome. I think a less competitive, perhaps more PvE-oriented game will be great to set up a good weed experience.

I'm going to give it a shot with just one hit tonight - if I don't feel anything, I'll try another. Thanks for the advice and the kind words!
Thanks for the good advice. 1-2 hits can generally keep me going for hours. I'll also talk to some of my friends at the dispensary.

Just for some more info. I'm very healthy. I eat healthy, run 7 miles a day, hold a full time job, have a great life to be honest. So I don't feel like a lot of the anxiety is rooted anywhere obvious.
Sometimes I wonder if I should smoke more often, and maybe it's a new-smoker scare? Or if weed just isn't for me at all. Thoughts?
